stops.note: 'happy, blessed, fortunate', from sǣl 'happiness'; German selig still means 'blessed'
slid from 'blessed' to 'innocent, harmless', then 'pitiable, helpless', as in the 'seely' sheep of medieval verse
sank to 'foolish'; journalists' 'silly season' for the trivial summer news of August and September dates from an 1861 article in The Saturday Review
